method.method_draft: Set up coordinates with P at the origin and the common angle bisector as the positive y-axis. Let one tangent ray have equation x=a y, with a>0. A circle tangent to both rays has its center on the y-axis, say at (0,c). If its tangent point on x=a y is distance s from P along the ray, projection of (0,c) onto the ray gives c=s*sqrt(1+a^2), and the radius equals the distance from (0,c) to the line x=a y, namely a c/sqrt(1+a^2)=a s. For the smaller circle, s=PA=4, so r=4a and its center height is 4sqrt(1+a^2). For the larger circle, s=PB=PA+AB=8, so R=8a and its center height is 8sqrt(1+a^2). Since the circles are externally tangent along the shared angle bisector, the distance between centers is 4sqrt(1+a^2), and this must equal R+r=12a. Hence sqrt(1+a^2)=3a, so 1+a^2=9a^2 and a^2=1/8. Therefore r^2=(4a)^2=16/8=2, giving area 2pi.
